author: East Houston News
title: Rep. Ed Case highlights veteran outreach and stance on government funding bills
text:
Rep. Ed Case, who represents Hawaii’s 1st district in the U.S. Congress, recently posted a series of updates on his official X account regarding his ongoing efforts to support veterans and address issues stemming from a government shutdown.
On November 9, 2025, Case shared details about a community event he hosted for veterans: “Yesterday I hosted my annual Special Veterans Talk Story community meeting at the O’ahu Veterans Center to report back on my actions in Congress on behalf of our vets, answer questions, listen to concerns and offer my assistance. Here’s a replay.”
Two days later, on November 10, 2025, Case described participating in a food distribution event aimed at supporting those affected by the shutdown and health care crisis: “As we strive to end this shutdown/health care crisis, I joined our Hawai’i Foodbank’s great volunteers at a special food distribution for our veterans, military and federal employees at Keehi Lagoon Memorial Park, with over 550 families coming thru for assistance.”
On November 12, 2025, Case addressed an upcoming vote on a continuing resolution (CR) intended to reopen the government: “After reviewing the details of the actual CR coming up for a vote and thinking it through, I’m voting no. I want to get government reopened, get our federal workers back to work and paid, and get programs like SNAP back underway. But this version cruelly and unnecessarily just”
Case has represented Hawaii’s 1st district since replacing Colleen Hanabusa in 2019. He previously served in the Hawaii House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002. Born in Hilo in 1952 and currently residing in Kāneʻohe, Case holds degrees from Williams College and UC Hastings Law School.
